result_semantic_payload.summary:
Both USDT transfers recorded in this device's logs are attributed, in the log lines themselves, to the account name "chenwei" on system A (/logs/app1.log): 2024-03-01 09:15:03 TRANSFER user=chenwei amount=30000USDT dest=TBait8888Wallet and 2024-03-02 22:43:55 TRANSFER user=chenwei amount=12000USDT dest=TBait8888Wallet, totalling 42,000 USDT to the same destination wallet. The log also shows chenwei LOGIN events bracketing each transfer (09:14:22 / 09:16:44 on 03-01; 22:41:10 on 03-02), and no TRANSFER event is attributed to any other account — liuyu's only event is a DOWNLOAD. On the second system (/logs/app2.log) there is also an account named "chenwei", but its activity (LOGIN, UPLOAD /shared/annual-plan.docx, PRINT to HQ-3F) contains no USDT transfer.

The evidence does NOT support treating the two same-named "chenwei" accounts as the same person. The device's own README states the two systems are unrelated internal systems that "share no account database"; the two logs use disjoint IP ranges (203.0.113.77 and 198.51.100.23 vs 10.20.0.5 and 10.20.0.9), non-overlapping date ranges (2024-03-01/02/05 vs 2024-02-20/21/22), and there is no shared identifier (no user ID, no hardware or device ID, no credential or token, no cross-system correlation key) linking the two accounts. Same-named accounts across independent systems are therefore only a name coincidence at best — identity equivalence is an unsupported inference.

Additional caveat on attribution itself: the logs are plain-text exports with no authentication evidence, no integrity hashes (md5 empty for all files) and no parser/attestation trail, so "user=chenwei" is an application-level log field, not proof that the person chenwei personally performed the transfer (session hijacking, shared or compromised credentials, and log tampering are all unexcluded). No Windows-native artifacts (Event Logs, Prefetch, Amcache, registry) are present in this task — only three plain files — so execution-level corroboration of the transfer actor is impossible here.
